king.name: King
queen.name: Queen
rook.name: Rook
bishop.name: Bishop
knight.name: Knight
pawn.name: Pawn
king.move: The king moves one square in any direction. It cannot move onto an attacked square.
queen.move: The queen moves any distance horizontally, vertically or diagonally. It cannot jump over pieces.
rook.move: The rook moves any distance horizontally or vertically. It cannot jump over pieces.
bishop.move: The bishop moves any distance diagonally. It stays on the same colour and cannot jump over pieces.
knight.move: The knight moves two squares in one direction and one to the side. It makes an L and can jump over pieces.
pawn.move: The pawn moves one square forward. On its first move it may move two if the path is clear. It captures one square diagonally forward. On the last rank it becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight.
board.body: A chessboard has 8 rows and 8 columns: 64 squares. The bottom-right square must be light.
turn.body: Each player starts with 16 pieces. White moves first. Players take turns making one move.
goal.body: The aim is to checkmate the other king. An attacked king is in check. If no legal move can escape the check, it is checkmate. Kings are never captured.
training.select: Select your piece, then tap a marked square.
training.free: Explore how your piece moves. This is a movement exercise.
training.capture: Use the {piece} to capture the opponent’s piece on {square}.
training.retry: Let’s try again. Select your piece, then move to the target square.
training.promoted: The pawn reached the last rank and became a queen in this exercise.
training.complete: You completed every task! You can play them again.
setup.intro: We see the board from White’s side. The bottom-right square is light. Place the white pieces first, then the black pieces.
setup.correct: Great! The piece is in the right place.
setup.retry: Try again. Check the piece name and tap the marked square.
setup.complete: The board is ready! Each side has 16 pieces. White moves first.
setup.queen: The queen starts on her own colour: the white queen on a light square, the black queen on a dark square.
setup.drag: Hold a piece and drag it to the marked square. You can also tap the piece and square.
safety.threat: An attacked king is in check. Find the black piece attacking the white king and tap it.
safety.escape: When in check, you must remove the threat. Select the king on e1 and move it to the safe square d1.
safety.capture: You can also protect the king by capturing the attacker. Select the bishop on h1 and capture the black rook on e4.
safety.block: You can block a distant attack. Select the rook on a2 and move it to e2 to protect your king.
safety.retry: Let’s try again. Look at the king with the red outline and listen to the instruction.
ending.title: Checkmate and Stalemate
ending.prompt: White to move. Choose the white king’s situation.
ending.mate.name: Checkmate
ending.stalemate.name: Stalemate
ending.check.name: Check, with an escape
ending.mate.body: The king is attacked and has no legal move. Checkmate! The game ends.
ending.stalemate.body: The king is not attacked but has no legal move. Stalemate! The game is a draw.
ending.check.body: The king is attacked but has a safe move. The game continues.
ending.retry: Look again: Is the king attacked? Is there a legal move?
mate.title: Mate in One
mate.prompt: White to move. Select a white piece and checkmate the black king in one move.
mate.correct: Great! The black king is attacked and has no legal escape. Checkmate!
mate.retry: This move does not give checkmate. Try another move.
opening.intro: An opening is the beginning of a game. Learn the ideas, then explore famous examples on the board.
opening.center: Use central pawns and pieces to control the middle. The four central squares are e4, d4, e5 and d5.
opening.develop: Bring knights and bishops into play. Usually, develop several pieces instead of moving the same one repeatedly.
opening.safety: Prepare to castle when it is legal and safe. Connect your rooks and avoid exposing your king.
opening.threats: Before every move, look for checks, captures and threats from both sides. An opening name does not make a move safe.
opening.italian.name: Italian Game
opening.italian.body: Develop the knight to f3 and bishop to c4. The bishop looks toward f7, while White prepares to castle. Black can answer in several ways.
opening.spanish.name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)
opening.spanish.body: The bishop goes to b5 and pressures the knight defending e5. Our example continues with a6, asking the bishop to decide where to go.
opening.scotch.name: Scotch Game
opening.scotch.body: White challenges the center early with d4. After the pawn exchange, the knight recaptures on d4 and takes an active central square.
opening.queens.name: Queen's Gambit
opening.queens.body: White offers the c-pawn to challenge Black's d5-pawn. Black can accept or decline; this example declines with e6 and develops pieces.
opening.london.name: London System
opening.london.body: White develops the dark-squared bishop to f4 before playing e3. Build a steady center, but adapt the plan to Black's moves.
opening.sicilian.name: Sicilian Defense
opening.sicilian.body: Black answers e4 with c5 to contest d4 from the side. This Open Sicilian example exchanges pawns and brings White's knight to d4.
opening.french.name: French Defense
opening.french.body: Black prepares d5 with e6. In this Advance Variation, White gains space with e5 and Black challenges the center with c5.
opening.caro.name: Caro-Kann Defense
opening.caro.body: Black prepares d5 with c6. In this example, Black captures on e4 and White recaptures with a knight; both sides still need to develop.
opening.step.center: This pawn move fights for control of the center and gives the pieces more room.
opening.step.develop: A minor piece joins the game and influences important squares.
opening.step.pressure: This move challenges an opposing piece or the opponent's control of the center.
opening.step.support: This pawn move supports the central structure or prepares another central pawn move.
opening.step.exchange: A capture changes the center. Notice which piece or pawn takes its place.
opening.step.space: The pawn advances to gain space. Check how the opponent can challenge the pawn chain.
